newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds slipped to a lower close in nervous low-volume trade on Friday after a firmer start, hurt by profit-taking.
Dealers said Thursday's profit-taking had left the market nervous, with guilder bonds failing to go all the way with rising bunds as the December DTB bund future contract hit a record high.
"There was a lot of supply in guilder bonds, despite the rosy futures picture," one dealer said. "The higher- than-expected Dutch October inflation figure added to that."
Dutch consumer prices picked up to 2.4 percent year-on-year.
The market had expected a 2.1 percent rise year on year.
"Let's say the CPI did not help matters, although generally speaking the market looks more to what is happening in Germany," a dealer said. "It's not really a problem," said another.

The 10-year six percent benchmark saw its discount to bunds narrow to nine basis points by midsession, but the yield gap widened again later to a more customary 11 points, compared with -12 basis points at Thursday's close.
One dealer noted some switching out of ten-year paper into shorter maturities, but said there had been little uptake for publisher Wolters Kluwer's 400 million seven-year issue.
